question: How does adjustment for measured baseline covariates change the observed smoking-cessation/weight-change contrast in the public NHEFS teaching cohort?
population: The 1,629 records in the author's public teaching release, restricted for this analysis to complete outcome and prespecified baseline covariates
time_zero: NHANES I baseline examination, 1971-1975; cessation status is only known over the interval to 1982
exposure: qsmk = 1, reported cessation between baseline and 1982
comparator: qsmk = 0, reported continued smoking over that interval
outcome: wt82_71, body-weight change from baseline to 1982, kg
estimand: Difference in normalized IP-weighted mean observed weight change between qsmk groups in the complete-case teaching sample
propensity_formula: qsmk ~ sex + race + age + I(age ** 2) + C(education) + smokeintensity + I(smokeintensity ** 2) + smokeyrs + I(smokeyrs ** 2) + C(exercise) + C(active) + wt71 + I(wt71 ** 2)
weights: 1/p for qsmk=1; 1/(1-p) for qsmk=0; normalize within exposure group for mean contrasts
missing_data: Complete-case illustration. Report every exclusion and group-specific missing outcome counts; do not equate missing follow-up with absence of an outcome.
identification_limits: Exact cessation time is not observed
Exchangeability given measured covariates is unverified
No causal effect is known from these observed data
diagnostics: standardized baseline differences before and after weighting

uncertainty.method: paired participant bootstrap, refitting the propensity model in every replicate

sensitivity_plan: Compare crude and weighted contrasts and balance. Revisit missing-outcome selection and alternative exposure timing before any causal interpretation. Within-sample bootstrap is not external validation.
